title: Rigor configuration
description: Configuration schema for `.rigor.yml` and `.rigor.dist.yml`. The committed default lives in `.rigor.dist.yml`; per-developer overrides live in `.rigor.yml` (gitignored). Path-bearing keys (`paths`, `signature_paths`, `plugins_io.allowed_paths`, `includes`) resolve relative to the config file that declares them. The full surface is documented at docs/handbook/01-getting-started.md.

includes.description: PHPStan-style include list. Each entry is a path to another `.rigor.yml`-shaped file whose body is merged under this one (later entries win on conflicts). Paths resolve relative to the file that declares them. Cycles are rejected.

target_ruby.description: Ruby version Rigor parses against (forwarded to `Prism.parse_file(version:)`). Format: `<major>.<minor>` or `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, or the literal `"latest"`.

paths.description: Files / directories to analyze. Directories are recursed; explicit files bypass the `exclude:` filter.

exclude.description: Glob patterns layered over directory globs. Built-in defaults — `**/vendor/bundle/**`, `**/.bundle/**`, `**/node_modules/**` — apply on top of user entries and cannot be disabled. Patterns use `File.fnmatch?` semantics (NOT regex).

plugins.description: Plugin gems Rigor loads. Each entry is either a String gem-name shorthand (`"rigor-deprecations"`) or a Hash with `gem:` / `id:` / `config:` keys for a configured plugin.

disable.description: Project-wide rule suppressions. Entries are canonical rule ids (`call.undefined-method`), legacy unprefixed names (`undefined-method`), or family wildcards (`call`, `flow`, `assert`, `dump`, `def`).

libraries.description: Bundled stdlib / stdgem RBS libraries to load (forwarded to `RBS::EnvironmentLoader#add(library:)`). Examples: `csv`, `set`, `pathname`.

signature_paths.description: Project-local RBS sig directories. `nil` (the default) lets `Environment.for_project` auto-detect a `sig/` directory.

pre_eval.description: ADR-17 — project-side monkey-patch pre-evaluation. Files listed here are walked BEFORE per-file inference so patched-method declarations are visible across the project (e.g. `lib/core_ext/string_extensions.rb`). Each entry resolves relative to the config file's directory; literal entries that don't exist surface as `pre-eval.file-not-found` (`:error`). Slice 4 (2026-05-16) accepts `File.fnmatch?`-shaped glob patterns (`lib/core_ext/**/*.rb`); a glob that matches nothing degrades silently to an empty entry (no diagnostic). Slices 1+2+3a have shipped registry + dispatcher tier + duplicate-declaration diagnostic; per-file cache descriptor (slice 3b) stays deferred until measured pain.

baseline.description: ADR-22 — path to the per-project baseline file (PHPStan-shaped). When set, `rigor check` loads the named file and filters known diagnostics per the WD4 ALL-or-NOTHING threshold semantics. `false` is the explicit-disable form (useful in `.rigor.yml` to override an upstream `.rigor.dist.yml`'s `baseline:` declaration). The convention path is `.rigor-baseline.yml` at the project root, but the path is loaded only when this key names it (WD2 (b) — file presence alone never activates the filter). Generate with `rigor baseline generate`.

fold_platform_specific_paths.description: When `true`, `File` path-manipulation methods fold to platform-aware constants (`File::SEPARATOR` etc.). Default `false` — most projects want platform-agnostic results.

parameter_inference.description: ADR-67 WD6 — opt-in call-site parameter type inference on the `check` walk. When `true`, `rigor check` runs a one-round pre-pass that types each undeclared `def` / `initialize` / setter parameter to the union of its resolved call-site argument types, sharpening downstream ivar reads, folds, narrowing, and protection coverage. Precision-additive only: the in-body negative rules (undefined-method, wrong-arity, argument-type-mismatch, possible-nil, visibility) decline on an inferred-parameter receiver/argument, because an open call-site union is a lower bound (WD6b). Default `false`, resolved off by every severity profile — a diagnostics-affecting activation is a compatibility change (ADR-50). Mutually exclusive with `--incremental` (WD6c).

effects.description: ADR-103 — effect labels. The PRESENCE of this block is the opt-in: `effects: {}` (or the bare key, which YAML parses as null) turns effect collection on with every sub-key at its default, and its absence keeps `rigor check` byte-identical and free. `false` is the explicit-disable form, useful in `.rigor.yml` to override an upstream `.rigor.dist.yml`'s block — the same shape `baseline:` uses. Nothing else enables collection: an `%a{rigor:v1:effect …}` or `%a{pure}` annotation in a project's RBS does not, because an annotation must not create a project-wide cost cliff. `rigor effects` runs under an implicit `effects: {}` when the key is absent. The sub-keys are DECLARED but not yet read — they land with their slices (#381 snapshot, #383 envelopes, #386 the declared lane), and reserving their shape first is the same discipline ADR-99 applies to a sibling implementation's namespace.

cache.description: On-disk cache settings. The cache stores parsed RBS environments, class ancestor tables, and plugin-side artefacts; deleting the directory is always safe (re-populates on next run).

max_bytes.description: LRU eviction cap for the cache directory, in bytes (ADR-54 WD3). Default 268435456 (256 MB). `null` disables eviction entirely, restoring the pre-ADR-54 unbounded store.

validation.description: How the cache decides a file is unchanged (ADR-87). `auto` (default) behaves as `digest` when a CI environment is detected — a fresh checkout regenerates every stat tuple, so stat validation cannot work there; `RIGOR_CI_DETECT=0` disables detection — and as `stat` otherwise. `stat` compares size + nanosecond mtime + inode and only re-hashes a file whose stat moved; `digest` re-hashes every file every run. Both keep the content hash as the sole change authority — `stat` only skips the hash when the stat proves the file untouched. `RIGOR_STRICT_VALIDATION=1` forces `digest` for one run and wins over this key.

plugins_io.description: Plugin I/O policy. `network: "disabled"` (default) makes `Plugin::IoBoundary#open_url` always raise. `network: "allowlist"` (v0.1.2) consults `allowed_url_hosts:` on every fetch — the URL must be HTTPS and the hostname must be on the list. `allowed_paths:` extends the default plugin read root (the project root) with extra absolute or relative paths.

network.description: Plugin network policy. `disabled` denies every URL fetch; `allowlist` permits HTTPS fetches whose hostname is in `allowed_url_hosts`.

allowed_paths.description: Extra read roots a plugin may access via `Plugin::IoBoundary`. Defaults to `[]` (project root only).

allowed_url_hosts.description: Hostnames a plugin may fetch via `Plugin::IoBoundary#open_url` while `network: allowlist`. Exact-match (no wildcards in v0.1.2). Plugins fetching a URL whose hostname is not on the list raise `AccessDeniedError`.

severity_profile.description: Profile that re-stamps each rule's authored severity. `lenient` flags the obvious bugs as errors and downgrades the rest to warnings; `balanced` (the default) follows Rigor's stance; `strict` upgrades every rule to error.

severity_overrides.description: Per-rule severity overrides applied after the profile. Keys are canonical rule ids (`call.undefined-method`) or family wildcards (`call`); values are one of `error` / `warning` / `info` / `off`. `off` drops the diagnostic entirely.

bleeding_edge.description: ADR-50 § WD2 — adopt the next major's queued diagnostic disciplines early. `false` (default) adopts none; `true` adopts the whole overlay; a list of feature ids adopts only those; `{ all: true, except: [ids] }` adopts all but the named. Orthogonal to `severity_profile:`. Inspect with `rigor show-bleedingedge`. The overlay is empty in this release, so every form is currently a no-op.

dependencies.description: Opt-in extensions to Rigor's outer inference boundary. Per ADR-10, `source_inference[]` lists gems whose Ruby implementation Rigor MAY walk when a signature contract is missing (or, in `mode: full`, alongside RBS). Inferred returns crossing the gem boundary are wrapped in `Dynamic[T]` with `dynamic.dependency-source.*` provenance — never published as ground-truth types and never round-tripped out as authored RBS. Omitted / empty = the existing RBS-or-`Dynamic[top]` boundary.

source_inference.description: Per-gem opt-in entries. Gems not listed keep the unlisted-gem default (no source walk).

budget_per_gem.description: Per-gem catalog cap (method-definition count). When the walker reaches this many catalog entries for a single gem, harvesting stops for that gem and Rigor surfaces a `dynamic.dependency-source.budget-exceeded` warning. Default 5000 (covers Rack, Faraday, Sidekiq); range 1250 – 20000 (0.25× – 4× of the default per ADR-10 § "Budget interaction").

budget_overrun_strategy.description: What the dispatcher should do for receivers in a budget-exceeded gem (ADR-10 5b). `walker_cap` (default, α): the walker stops harvesting at the cap; methods past the cap fall through to the engine's user-class fallback path. `dependency_silence` (β): same walker behaviour, but the dispatcher additionally returns `Dynamic[top]` for any call on a class belonging to a budget-exceeded gem (silences `call.undefined-method` for unrecorded methods at the cost of weaker static checking on that gem's surface).

parallel.description: ADR-15 — opt-in parallel analysis. When `workers` is greater than zero, `rigor check` dispatches per-file analysis across N worker processes (the fork-based pool is the active backend; the Ractor pool is deferred). Default `0` keeps the sequential path. The CLI's `--workers=N` flag and the `RIGOR_RACTOR_WORKERS` env var both override this setting; precedence is CLI > env > config > 0. Applies to `--incremental` re-checks as well as full runs.

workers.description: Number of parallel workers. `0` (default) runs sequentially; `N > 0` dispatches per-file analysis across N forked workers.

bundler.description: Open item O4 — target-project Bundler awareness. When `bundle_path:` is set (or `auto_detect:` succeeds), Rigor walks `<bundle_path>/ruby/*/gems/*/sig/` and adds each gem-shipped sig directory to the loader's `signature_paths`. Conflicts with rigor's bundled stdlib RBS degrade gracefully to `Dynamic[top]` with a one-line warning (per the O7 failure-memo in `RbsLoader#env`).

bundle_path.description: Explicit path to the bundler install root (relative paths resolve from the project root). Typical values: `"vendor/bundle"` for an in-tree install, or an absolute path for a Docker-mounted bundle. When `null` (default) and `auto_detect` is true, Rigor reads `.bundle/config`'s `BUNDLE_PATH:` and falls back to `vendor/bundle/`.

auto_detect.description: When `bundle_path` is unset, search `.bundle/config` and `vendor/bundle/` under the project root. Setting `false` disables bundle sig discovery entirely.

lockfile.description: Explicit path to a `Gemfile.lock` (O4 Layer 3 slice 1). When set (or auto-detected next to the project root via the `auto_detect:` flag), Rigor parses the lockfile and FILTERS the bundle-discovered `sig/` directories so only gems whose `(name, version, platform)` matches a lockfile entry are admitted. Stale gems left in the bundle install tree (out-of-band installs, version drift after `bundle update`) are silently dropped.

rigor_rs.description: RESERVED — declared here, never read by this implementation. A sibling implementation (`rigor-rs`) groups its own keys under this namespace so one `.rigor.yml` feeds both; reference-schema keys stay top-level for parity. This implementation type-checks the shape at schema level ONLY: it never reads, validates, or coerces the value, and never errors on it however invalid. The reservation is authoritative, so an undeclared key here is an error — a sibling key is reserved in this schema BEFORE the sibling implements it. See docs/internal-spec/config.md and ADR-99.

ruby.description: The sibling's Ruby-sidecar coverage posture. One of the reserved keywords `require` / `auto` / `off`, or a path to a ruby binary (any other string is read as a path; use a path form such as `./off` to name a ruby colliding with a keyword). Deliberately unconstrained beyond `string` — an enum would reject every path form. This implementation has no sidecar concept and ignores the key entirely.

rbs_collection.description: Open item O4 Layer 3 slice 2 — `rbs collection install` awareness. When the target project has been set up with `rbs collection install`, the resulting `rbs_collection.lock.yaml` records resolved (gem, version, source) triples and `.gem_rbs_collection/<name>/<version>/` carries the downloaded `.rbs` files. Rigor parses the lockfile and auto-feeds each gem's directory into the loader's `signature_paths`. `stdlib`-typed entries are skipped (rigor's bundled `DEFAULT_LIBRARIES` already covers them).

lockfile.description: Explicit path to `rbs_collection.lock.yaml` (relative paths resolve from the project root). When `null` (default) and `auto_detect` is true, Rigor looks for `<project_root>/rbs_collection.lock.yaml`.

auto_detect.description: When `lockfile` is unset, search for `rbs_collection.lock.yaml` under the project root. Setting `false` disables collection-sig discovery entirely.

effectsBlock.description: The body of the `effects:` opt-in. `snapshot:` and `tolerated:` are read (the effect snapshot, #381); the rest are reserved — declared, accepted, and not yet read by this implementation.

check.description: Whether authored envelopes (`%a{pure}`, `%a{rigor:v1:effect …}`) are checked against the collected summaries. Default `true`. NOT READ YET — the envelope reader lands with #383.

snapshot.description: The committed effect snapshot and its drift gate — `rigor effects update` / `check` / `diff` / `explain` (ADR-103 WD7). READ.

reach.description: Entry points whose TRANSITIVE footprint the snapshot records under `reach:`. Each entry is either a file glob — anything carrying a path or glob character, matched project-relative with the `unused --entry-point` semantics (`File.fnmatch?` with `FNM_PATHNAME`, so `**` is the only way across a directory boundary) — or the bare name of an entry-point preset a plugin registered. An unknown preset name is a load-time error. Default `[]` — `methods:` only.

gate.description: What `rigor effects check` treats as drift. `symmetric` (default) reports removals too — a job that stopped enqueueing is news; `additions` is the ratchet option.

labels.description: Project-owned vocabulary extensions, layered over `data/effects/registry.yml`. A project may open any root. NOT READ YET.

attribution.description: Per-gem effect attribution: `{ gem-or-method-key: [labels] }` for third-party code Rigor cannot see. Attributed labels never discharge a taint — they read as "declared this, and possibly more" (ADR-103 WD6). NOT READ YET.

envelopes.description: Envelopes by convention rather than by annotation — the ADR-28 path/namespace shape. Each entry bounds the methods it selects. NOT READ YET — lands with #383.

tolerated.description: Labels a judgment discharges by policy. Read by the snapshot gate: a `rigor effects check` difference confined to tolerated labels is reported under a `tolerated:` heading and does not fail (`--strict-tolerated` makes it fail, `--no-tolerated-effects` judges as if the list were empty). The snapshot RECORD is undischarged either way. Label SHAPE is validated at load; a label the registry does not know is `effect.unknown-label`'s business, not an error. Per-origin discharge — a bundle is discharged when ANY of its labels is tolerated, because tolerating what an origin was FOR frees the transport it came with (ADR-103 WD14) — arrives with the envelope slices.

views.description: Whether view templates are analysed as effect units (ADR-103 WD11). Default `false`. NOT READ YET.

effectEnvelopeEntry.description: One convention envelope: the methods it selects, and the bound it puts on them.

match.description: Path glob the envelope applies to.

namespace.description: Constant namespace the envelope applies to.

effect.description: The bound: a list of labels, or the empty list for `pure`.

gem.description: Gem name (matched against the bundle at walk time).

mode.description: `when_missing` (default): walk gem source ONLY when no signature contract resolves for the call site. `full`: walk even when RBS is present; the analyzer reconciles via the contribution-merging rules in ADR-2 (RBS still wins on conflict). `disabled`: explicitly opt out (matches the unlisted-gem default).

roots.description: Subdirectories within the gem's installation directory to walk. Defaults to `["lib"]`. C extensions and `spec/` / `test/` / `bin/` are hard-excluded by the loader regardless of this setting (per ADR-10).

pluginEntry.description: A single plugin entry — either a gem-name shorthand or the full configured form.

oneOf.description: Gem-name shorthand, e.g. `rigor-deprecations`. The id defaults to the gem name without the `rigor-` prefix.

id.description: Plugin id, used as the `source_family` prefix in diagnostics (`plugin.<id>.<rule>`). Defaults to the gem name without the `rigor-` prefix.

config.description: Plugin-specific configuration. Validated by the plugin's `manifest(config_schema:)`. The shape varies per plugin; see each plugin's README for the recognised keys.

enabled.description: Set `false` to opt a listed plugin out entirely — it is neither required, trusted, nor loaded. The intended use (ADR-93 WD2) is disabling the `rigor-rbs-inline` plugin that Rigor auto-wires by default when the upstream `rbs-inline` library is resolvable. Defaults to `true`.
